entities.summary: Sebastianus, a brother of Jovinus, was an aristocrat of southern Gaul who rose to prominence after his brother usurped the throne of the western Roman Emperor Honorius in Gaul in 411. After Jovinus named Sebastianus as Augustus (co-emperor) in 412, coins bearing Sebastianus' image were minted at Arles and Trier, solidifying his power and influence in the region. Sebastianus' reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Visigoths and Vandals, which he won with the help of his brother Jovinus. However, their victory was short-lived, as the brothers were defeated and killed by the Visigoths in 415. Despite his relatively short time as co-emperor, Sebastianus left a lasting legacy in the region, with his image appearing on coins and monuments for centuries to come. This legacy is a testament to the enduring power of the Roman Empire, even in the face of internal strife and external threats. As a symbol of the Roman aristocracy, Sebastianus represents the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the late Roman Empire.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sebastianus' reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Visigoths and Vandals, which he won with the help of his brother Jovinus. Despite their victory, the brothers were defeated and killed by the Visigoths in 415.
